title: Sepsis Recognition: Perfusion, Lactate and Organ Dysfunction
subject: Emergency Triage
preview: Sepsis is life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated response to infection, not simply a positive blood culture.
quickRevision: Sepsis is life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated response to infection, not simply a positive blood culture.
Elevated lactate can support concern for impaired perfusion but also has nonhypoxic causes; it is not a stand-alone sepsis test.
Early recognition, cultures when feasible without delaying care, source control and appropriate antimicrobials are core principles.

sections.title: Recognize the situation
points: Sepsis is life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated response to infection, not simply a positive blood culture.
Look for altered mentation, low blood pressure, reduced urine output, respiratory distress and poor perfusion.

sections.title: Clinical decisions & differential
points: Elevated lactate can support concern for impaired perfusion but also has nonhypoxic causes; it is not a stand-alone sepsis test.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not wait for fever or a positive culture before recognizing possible sepsis.

quiz.question: Which is central to the modern concept of sepsis?
options: A positive culture in every case
